lease.dated: March 14, 2013 (amended March 11, 2016; January 23, 2018; June 25, 2019; letter agreement fixing Third Amendment Effective Date as June 28, 2019)
lease.premises: Originally a portion of the 21st floor, 152 West 57th Street a/k/a Carnegie Hall Tower, New York; replaced by a portion of the 10th floor (Second Amendment) plus Additional Premises on the 10th floor (Third Amendment)
lease.tenant: Thorne Research, Inc., an Idaho corporation

positions.lease_says: Transfers need Owner's consent, with a recapture right and a 50 percent share of sublease profit and assignment consideration, but Tenant may transfer without consent to affiliates, subsidiaries and successors and may defeat recapture by withdrawing its request.
positions.proposed_response: Apply the net worth test in Article 52(g) to affiliate and subsidiary transfers as well as successors, require that any affiliate or subsidiary transferee remain an affiliate or subsidiary for the transfer to stay valid, and delete Tenant's right in Article 52(a)(2) to rescind its request after Owner elects recapture.
quotes: Owner may notify Tenant that Owner elects to: (a) cancel this lease, in which event such cancellation shall become effective on the date proposed by Tenant for such assignment or subletting
Tenant shall have the right to rescind the Tenant request to assign the Lease or sublease the Premises which gave rise to such exercise by Owner

Tenant may, without Owner’s consent and on not less than ten (10) days prior written notice to Owner, ... assign this lease or sublet the demised premises to, or otherwise permit the use of the demised premises by, an entity into which Tenant is merged or consolidated or to an entity which shall be an “affiliate”, “subsidiary” or “successor”
positions.why: Recapture and the 50 percent profit share match the standard, but the net worth test applies only to successors, so affiliate and subsidiary transfers are consent-free with no financial test. Article 52(h) also lets up to two affiliate Permitted Users occupy up to 25 percent without consent, and Tenant can nullify a recapture election by rescinding within five days.

positions.lease_says: The premises may be used only for general and executive offices and for no other purpose.
quotes: General and executive offices and for no other purpose.
Tenant shall use and occupy the demised premises only for the Permitted Use as set forth in the Basic Lease Provisions Section of this lease and for no other purpose.
positions.why: Use is limited to office use with no other purpose allowed, which matches the standard.

positions.lease_says: All alterations need Owner's prior written consent and Owner-approved contractors, but Owner may not unreasonably withhold or delay consent for interior, non-structural work that does not affect Building systems.
positions.proposed_response: Delete Note 1 so Owner's consent to all non-decorative alterations is in its discretion. If a reasonableness standard is kept, limit it to work under a small per-project cost cap that does not touch structure or Building systems.
quotes: Tenant shall, make no changes in or to the demised premises of any nature without Owner’s prior written consent.

which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed in the case of interior, non-structural work to be performed wholly within the demised premises, which work does not affect the proper functioning of any Building system or equipment
positions.why: Consent is still required and review costs are reimbursed under Article 59, but Note 1 puts Owner under a reasonableness standard for all interior non-structural work regardless of cost, which leaves Owner discretion only for structural or system work. The filed Notes do not show where Note 1 is inserted; it appears to attach to the Article 3 consent requirement.

positions.lease_says: Tenant must remove specialty alterations and repair the resulting damage at its cost unless Owner agreed in writing, at Tenant's request when consent was sought, that removal would not be required.
quotes: unless Owner shall agree to the contrary in writing following Tenant’s specific request as to whether Tenant shall be required to remove the proposed alteration

Tenant shall be required to remove, no later than thirty (30) days prior to the Expiration Date or earlier termination of the Term, any vaults and raised floors, kitchens, kitchen appliances and pantries, staircases, antennas or any other “specialty” installations or alterations
positions.why: Removal is the default, and Owner does not need to designate items at the time of consent. This matches or exceeds the standard.

positions.lease_says: Tenant pays its proportionate share of operating expense increases over a base year (reset to calendar 2019 by the Third Amendment), with no cap, and expenses are grossed up to 95 percent occupancy.
quotes: equal to Tenant’s Proportionate Share of the Operating Expenses for the then current Lease Year or calendar year (as the case may be) that are in excess of the Operating Expenses for the Operating Base Year
Operating Expenses for such period shall be adjusted to reflect Operating Expenses that would have been incurred if ninety-five percent (95%) of the rentable space in the Building had been occupied.
the Operating Base Year (as defined in the Basic Lease Provisions) shall be the calendar year 2019
positions.why: There is no cap, and there is no gross-up of the base year in Tenant's favor. This matches the standard.

positions.lease_says: Because no actual real estate taxes are payable, Tenant pays its proportionate share of the increase in assessed value times tax rate over a Tax Base, with the base year reset to fiscal 2019/20 by the Third Amendment.
quotes: In lieu of a real estate tax escalation, Tenant hereby covenants and agrees to pay to Owner as additional rent on the first day of each and every month during the Term an amount equal to the quotient obtained by dividing the amount of the Taxes applicable to the then current Lease Year by the number of months in such Lease Year.
Fiscal year July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.
If the Tax Base is at any time reduced for any reason whatsoever, Owner shall have the right to adjust the amount of each of Tenant’s payments previously made on account of Taxes
sections: Article 37(a)(iii) (as amended by Third Amendment Paragraph 4(C))
positions.why: This is a proportionate share of increases over a base tax year, and Owner may recapture if the Tax Base is reduced. That matches the standard, though the charge is computed from assessed value rather than taxes actually paid.

positions.lease_says: Tenant posts cash security, now $220,619.00, which Owner may apply on default; Tenant may substitute an unconditional letter of credit; there is no burn-down.
quotes: it is agreed that in the event Tenant defaults in respect of any of the terms, provisions and conditions of this lease
Owner may present such letter of credit for payment upon the occurrence of any default by Tenant hereunder beyond the expiration of any applicable notice or grace period set forth herein
thereby increasing the cash security held by Landlord under the Lease to $220,619.00
positions.why: Cash or an unconditional letter of credit is required and there is no reduction. Draws on the letter of credit require a default past notice and cure, which the standard permits.

positions.lease_says: Tenant carries general liability insurance of at least $3,000,000 per occurrence naming Owner and its managing agent as additional insureds, and both parties waive recovery to the extent of their insurance.
positions.proposed_response: Raise Tenant's commercial general liability limit to not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence (primary plus umbrella), keeping Owner and its managing agent as additional insureds.
quotes: naming Owner (as that term was broadly defined for purposes of this Article only) and Owner’s current managing agent, TF Cornerstone Inc., and any future managing agent, as additional insureds
in limits (subject to increase at Owner’s reasonable request) of not less than $3,000,000 combined single limit for bodily and personal injury or death and for property damage per occurrence
Tenant hereby waives any and all right of recovery which it might otherwise have against Owner
positions.why: The $3,000,000 limit is below the $5 million standard, although Owner may reasonably request increases. The additional insured and mutual waiver terms match the standard.

positions.lease_says: Tenant indemnifies Owner broadly for claims arising from its use and control of the premises and from acts of its people; Owner gives no general indemnity.
quotes: covenants and agrees to indemnify and hold Owner harmless from and against all claims, actions, judgments, damages, liabilities or expenses including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys’ fees, in connection with damage to property or injury or death to persons, arising from or out of the use, alteration, occupation, management, possession or control of the demised premises
Tenant shall indemnify and save harmless Owner against and from all liabilities, obligations, damages, penalties, claims, costs and expenses for which Owner shall not be reimbursed by insurance
positions.why: Tenant's indemnity is broad and not limited to gross negligence, and Owner's only indemnities are the mutual broker indemnities in the amendments. This matches the standard.

positions.lease_says: Recovery against Owner is limited to its estate and interest in the Building, and Owner is never liable for consequential damages on injury and property-loss claims.
quotes: Tenant shall look only to Owner’s estate and interest in the Building for the satisfaction of Tenant’s remedies

provided, however, that even if due to any such gross negligence of Owner or Owner’s agents, in no event shall any of the Indemnitees ever be liable with respect to any claim for consequential damages in connection therewith
positions.why: The non-recourse limit matches the standard. The consequential damages bar sits in Article 43(c), which addresses injury and property loss, and is not stated as a general bar for every claim.

positions.lease_says: After a default notice, Tenant appears to have 10 days to cure monetary defaults and 20 days (extended while diligently curing) for other defaults, after which Owner must serve a second five-day cancellation notice.
positions.proposed_response: Provide that the lease may be terminated on expiration of the cure period under a single default notice, deleting the separate five-day cancellation notice, and confirm cure periods of 10 days after notice for monetary defaults and no more than 30 days, extended only for diligent cure, for other defaults.
quotes: upon Owner serving a written fifteen (15) days’ notice upon Tenant specifying the nature of said default)
then Owner may serve a written five (5) days’ notice of cancellation of this lease upon Tenant
in the case of default not involving the payment of a money or ten (10) days in the case of any default involving the payment of money
positions.why: The cure periods appear within the standard, but termination requires a second (cancellation) notice. The filed Notes do not show where they are inserted, so the exact cure periods (Note 11 "twenty (20)" appears to replace the printed 15 days) and whether rent defaults now need notice cannot be confirmed.

positions.lease_says: Owner repairs casualty damage, rent abates only for the unusable part (or fully if wholly unusable), only Owner may terminate, and Tenant waives its statutory termination right.
quotes: shall be apportioned from the day following the casualty, according to e part of the demised premises which is usable
Owner may elect to terminate this lease by written notice to Tenant
Tenant hereby waives the provisions of Section 227 of the Real Property Law
positions.why: Tenant has no termination right and abatement is tied to usable space. This matches or exceeds the standard.

positions.lease_says: A holdover Tenant pays 250 percent of the last year's Base Rent and additional rent and is liable from day one for all of Owner's losses, including succeeding tenants' claims.
quotes: per diem use and occupancy in respect of the demised premises equal to two and one-half (2 1/2) times the Base Rent and additional rent payable hereunder for the last year of the Term
(i) all losses and damages which Owner may incur or sustain by reason thereof
positions.why: The rate exceeds 150 percent and damages liability has no grace period. This is more favorable to Owner than the standard.

positions.lease_says: The lease and amendments grant no renewal, expansion, first-offer or termination options; term extensions were made only by negotiated amendments, and any option is unexercisable during a default.
quotes: Tenant shall not be entitled to exercise any right of termination or other option granted to it by this lease (if any) at any time when Tenant is in default
positions.why: No options are granted, which matches the standard.

positions.lease_says: New York law governs, and both parties waive jury trial except for personal injury or property damage claims.
quotes: This lease shall be governed in all respects by the internal laws of the State of New York.

the respective parties hereto shall, and they hereby do, waive trial by jury in any action proceeding or counterclaim brought by either of the parties hereto against the other (except for personal injury or property damage)
positions.why: New York law governs and the jury waiver is mutual, which matches the standard; the personal injury and property damage carve-out is the standard printed-form exception.

lease.premises: Entire seventh (7th) floor, 44 West 37th Street, New York, New York

positions.lease_says: Transfers need Landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, with a recapture right (12.C), a 50% profit share (12.J), a merger/asset-sale exception with a net worth test (12.K), a consent-free affiliate transfer with no net worth test (12.L), and deemed consent if Landlord does not respond within 30 days.
positions.proposed_response: Condition the Section 12.L affiliate transfer on a net worth test and advance delivery of proof, as in 12.K. Delete the deemed consent in 12.G, or require a second notice with bold-face warning before consent is deemed given. Extend the recapture right in 12.C to any sublease of 50% or more of the Premises.
quotes: without obtaining the prior written consent of Landlord in each instance, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

Tenant may, without Landlord's consent, but upon written notice to Landlord, permit any corporations or other business entities (but not including Governmental Entities) which control, are controlled by, or are under common control with Tenant (herein referred to as "related corporation") to receive an assignment of this Lease or to sublet all or part of the Premises
in the event Landlord fails to respond within such thirty (30) day period, Landlord’s consent to the proposed assignment or sublease shall be deemed granted.
positions.why: Recapture, the 50% profit share and the merger net worth test match the standard. However, the affiliate transfer needs no consent and carries no net worth test, and the deemed-consent mechanism goes beyond the standard position. Recapture also applies only to an assignment or a sublet for substantially the balance of the Term.

positions.lease_says: The Premises may be used only for general, executive and administrative offices and for no other purpose.
quotes: "Permitted Uses" shall mean general, executive and administrative office use only.
Tenant agrees to use and occupy the Premises for the Permitted Uses, and for no other purpose.
positions.why: Matches the standard position word for word.

positions.lease_says: Alterations need Landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Cosmetic work under $50,000 per project or six-month series needs no consent. Review costs are capped at $3,500, and plans are deemed approved after 15 days of silence.
positions.proposed_response: Limit consent-free work to purely decorative painting and carpeting, or cap Minor Alterations at a small per-project amount (for example $10,000) excluding anything touching building systems or structure. Delete the $3,500 cap on review costs. Replace deemed approval with a second-notice mechanism.
quotes: Tenant shall not be required to obtain Landlord’s consent for repainting, recarpeting, or other alterations, tenant improvements, alterations or physical additions to the Premises which are cosmetic in nature totaling less than $50,000 in any single instance or series of related alterations performed within a six-month period (“Minor Alterations”)

shall pay to Landlord all costs and expenses reasonably incurred by Landlord (including the cost of Landlord's Consultant) in connection with Landlord's review of Tenant's plans and specifications, capped at $3,500.00

In the event Landlord fails to respond to Tenant's request for consent to Alterations within fifteen (15) days of Tenant's submission to Landlord of Tenant's plans, said plans ... shall deemed to be approved by Landlord
positions.why: The consent-free category reaches $50,000, which is well above a low threshold. Landlord's review-cost recovery is capped, and silence counts as approval, so the clause gives Tenant more than the standard position.

positions.lease_says: Tenant must remove Specialty Alterations at its cost before expiration and repair the damage, without any designation by Landlord at the time of consent.
quotes: Tenant shall be obligated to remove Specialty Alterations from the Premises, at Tenant's expense, prior to the Expiration Date.

“Specialty Alterations” shall include Alterations consisting of kitchens, pantries, executive bathrooms, computer installations, safe deposit boxes, vaults, libraries or file rooms requiring reinforcement of floors, internal staircases, conveyors, dumbwaiters and other Alterations of a similar character, which would be unusually difficult and expensive to remove and are not typical for normal office space
positions.why: The removal duty does not depend on Landlord's designation, which matches the standard. Raised floors and supplemental HVAC are not expressly listed and fall in only through the 'similar character' catch-all.

positions.lease_says: The escalation article covers only real estate taxes, so Tenant pays no operating expense escalation.
positions.proposed_response: Add an operating expense escalation under which Tenant pays its 9% Proportionate Share of increases over a base year, with no cap on controllable expenses.
quotes: “Additional Rent” shall mean the amounts payable by Tenant on account of Tenant’s Proportionate Share of Taxes as described in Article 28 herein, the Electric Charges as described in Article 30 herein, and all other amounts expressly identified as being Additional Rent payable by Tenant to Landlord under this Lease.

If the Taxes payable for any Comparison Year (any part or all of which falls within the Term) shall represent an increase above the Base Taxes, then the Rent for such Comparison Year ... shall be increased by Tenant's Proportionate Share of such increase.
positions.why: Tenant pays no share of operating expense increases, which is a listed departure. Tenant does separately bear its own cleaning, HVAC unit maintenance, window cleaning and submetered electricity.

positions.lease_says: Tenant pays its 9% Proportionate Share of tax increases over the 2023/2024 Base Tax Year, and the Base Taxes are not reduced if the base assessment is later lowered.
quotes: "Base Tax Year" shall mean the Taxes payable for the 2023/2024 Tax Year (as defined in Article 28 hereof).

the Assessed Valuation which had been utilized in computing the Base Taxes is reduced (as a result of settlement, final determination of legal proceedings or otherwise) then, and in such event the Base Taxes shall not be reduced to reflect such reduction.
positions.why: Matches the standard and protects the base year from reduction. The only point to note is that Tenant is relieved of a year's escalation if Landlord does not deliver a statement within three years (28.C(i)).

positions.lease_says: Tenant posts an $80,000 deposit in cash or as a clean, unconditional letter of credit. Landlord may draw after an Event of Default, and there is no burn-down.
quotes: Tenant shall deliver to Landlord the Security Deposit in the form of either a cash deposit (the “Cash Deposit”) or a letter of credit (the “Letter of Credit”).

In the Event of a Default, in addition to any or all of its other remedies contained in this Lease, Landlord shall have the right (but not the obligation) to draw down on the Cash Deposit or present the Letter of Credit for payment and to draw thereon, in whole or in part.
positions.why: Cash or an unconditional letter of credit with a draw right after a default following notice and cure is the standard position, and the absence of any reduction is better for Landlord.

positions.lease_says: Tenant carries commercial general liability insurance of $3,000,000 per occurrence, names Landlord and its managing agent as additional insureds, and the waiver of subrogation is mutual.
positions.proposed_response: Increase the commercial general liability requirement to not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence, which may be met through primary plus umbrella or excess coverage.
quotes: The minimum limits of liability shall be a combined single limit with respect to each occurrence in an amount of not less than $3,000,000.00 per occurrence.

Landlord, Landlord's managing agent, the present and any future mortgagee of the Real Property or the Building and/or such other designees specified by Landlord, from time to time, as additional insureds
Landlord and Tenant each waives any claim it might have against the other
positions.why: The liability limit is below the $5,000,000 standard. The additional-insured and mutual waiver provisions are consistent.

positions.lease_says: Tenant gives a broad indemnity for its acts, the Premises and its breaches, while Landlord indemnifies Tenant for Losses from any act, omission or negligence of Landlord or its agents, contractors or employees and from Landlord's breach.
positions.proposed_response: Limit Landlord's indemnity in 37.B to Losses caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Landlord or its agents, contractors or employees, subject to 9.C and Article 16.
quotes: Landlord shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Tenant and its representatives and agents from and against each and every Loss arising out of any act, omission or negligence of Landlord, or any of its agents, contractors or employees
positions.why: Landlord's indemnity reaches any act or omission, not only negligence or willful misconduct. The 'and' linking it to Landlord's breach makes the scope ambiguous.

positions.lease_says: Landlord's liability is limited to direct damages recoverable only from its interest in the Building and Real Property, and neither party is liable for consequential damages except under Article 21.
quotes: The liability of Landlord for Landlord's obligations under this Lease shall not exceed and shall be limited to Tenant's actual direct, but not consequential, damages therefor and shall only be recoverable from Landlord's interest in the Building and the Real Property
In no event shall Landlord or Tenant ... ever be liable for incidental or consequential damages, except as provided in Article 21 herein.
positions.why: Matches the standard. The consequential-damages waiver is mutual, but the Article 21 carve-out preserves Tenant's holdover exposure.

positions.lease_says: Tenant has 10 days after notice to cure monetary defaults and 30 days after notice for other defaults, extended only while Tenant diligently pursues a cure.
quotes: if Tenant shall default in the payment when due of any installment of Rent or in the payment when due of any Additional Rent, and such default shall continue for a period of ten (10) days following written notice from Landlord to Tenant; or

Tenant shall fail to remedy such default within thirty (30) days after notice by Landlord to Tenant of such default, or if such default is of such a nature that it cannot be completely remedied within said period of thirty (30) days and Tenant shall not commence within said period of thirty (30) days, or shall not thereafter diligently prosecute to completion all steps necessary to remedy such default
positions.why: Within the standard 5-to-10-day and 30-day periods with a diligence condition and a single default notice. The 10-day termination notice is the usual conditional limitation.

positions.lease_says: Tenant may terminate if repairs are estimated to take, or actually take, more than 180 days, or if the casualty occurs in the final Lease Year, and rent abates for the untenantable portion.
positions.proposed_response: Extend Tenant's termination trigger to 12 months, both for Landlord's estimate and for actual completion. Limit the final-Lease-Year right to material damage that cannot be repaired within a stated period (for example 90 days).
quotes: Landlord estimates that the damage caused thereby cannot be repaired within one hundred eighty (180) days after the commencement of repairs (the "Repair Period"), or if in fact the damage is not actually fully repaired by Landlord within one hundred eighty (180) days of the date of occurrence of the Casualty, or if the Casualty occurs during the final Lease Year then Tenant may terminate this Lease
rent for the portion of the Premises rendered untenantable by the damage shall be abated on a reasonable basis
positions.why: The 180-day trigger, and the final-year trigger with no stated threshold, are well short of the 12-month standard. The abatement is properly limited to the untenantable portion.

positions.lease_says: Holdover base Rent is 150% for the first 30 days and 200% thereafter, with Additional Rent at 100%, and Tenant indemnifies for succeeding-tenant claims and lost profits after 30 days.
quotes: a sum equal to (i) one and one-half (1.5) times the aggregate of that portion of the Rent for the first 30 days of such holdover, and 100% of the Additional Rent which was payable under this Lease during the last month of the Term, and (ii) two (2) times the aggregate of that portion of the Rent for any time thereafter

if Tenant shall hold-over or remain in possession of any portion of the Premises for more than thirty (30) days following the Expiration Date, Tenant shall protect, defend, indemnify and hold Landlord harmless from all loss, costs (including reasonable attorneys' fees) and liability resulting from such failure, including any claims made by any succeeding tenant founded upon such failure to surrender, and any lost profits to Landlord resulting therefrom.
positions.why: The 150% rising to 200% schedule and the post-grace damages exposure meet the standard. Additional Rent is held at 100%, and 'that portion of the Rent' is not tied expressly to the last month's rate.

positions.lease_says: Tenant has a one-time option to terminate effective at the end of the month after the second anniversary of the Commencement Date, on six months' notice and payment of a three-month fee; the option is personal and unavailable during an Event of Default; there is no renewal or expansion right.
positions.proposed_response: Confirm with the client that the Termination Option is approved. Require that no Event of Default exist both on the notice date and on the Termination Date. Confirm that the three-month fee covers Landlord's unamortized costs, including Landlord's Work and brokerage commissions, or increase it accordingly.
quotes: Provided no Event of Default has occurred under this Lease beyond the expiration of all applicable grace and/or cure periods expressly set forth herein, Tenant shall have a one-time option to terminate this Lease (the “Termination Option”).

Tenant must pay to Landlord, by wire transfer, a termination fee equal to three (3) months of the then escalated Rent and Additional Rent due from Tenant as of the Termination Date (the “Termination Fee”).
The Termination Option is reserved to Tenant and will not inure to the benefit of any sublessees, transferees, successors and/or assigns of Tenant.
positions.why: Any early termination right is a departure unless the partner confirms it was approved. It is personal and conditioned on no Event of Default, but only at the time the option is exercised.

positions.lease_says: New York law governs, with venue in New York County, and both parties waive trial by jury.
quotes: This Lease shall be deemed to have been made in New York County, New York, and shall be construed in accordance with the laws of New York.

It is mutually agreed by and between Landlord and Tenant that the respective parties hereto shall and they hereby do waive trial by jury in any action, proceeding or counterclaim brought by either of the parties hereto against the other on any matters whatsoever arising out of or in any way connected with this Lease
positions.why: Matches the standard position.

lease.premises: Entire 60th floor (deemed 26,363 rentable square feet), One Vanderbilt Avenue, New York, New York

positions.lease_says: Article 4 (Assignment/Subletting) is redacted in full as "4.01[***]", so the operative assignment and subletting terms cannot be read.
positions.why: The point cannot be tested against the standard because the text is redacted. The defined-terms index refers to "Leaseback Area" (4.02), "Affiliate" (4.10(a)) and "controls" (4.10(b)), which suggests a recapture right and a consent-free affiliate or control-transfer exception. Their terms, and any profit-sharing split, are not visible.

positions.lease_says: Use is limited to executive and general office, plus an open-ended list of ancillary uses for Permitted Users that includes data centers, printing, conference centers, an exercise facility, recording and video studios, and serving alcohol.
positions.proposed_response: Delete "without limitation" so the ancillary uses are a closed list of specifically approved exceptions. Confirm that any ancillary use not listed requires Landlord's prior written consent.
quotes: Such ancillary uses may include, without limitation, the following uses, provided the same are (x) ancillary to the primary use of the Premises for executive and general offices
Tenant may serve (but not sell) in the Premises alcoholic beverages solely to Permitted Users and not to the general public

recording and video studios (provided that Tenant shall cause such recording and video studios to be operated and constructed so that no noise or vibration will emanate from the Premises to other portions of the Building)
positions.why: The core use is general office, and cooking is barred. However, the "without limitation" ancillary list goes beyond general office to include studios, an exercise facility, conference centers and alcohol service, and it is not a closed list of approved exceptions.

positions.lease_says: Landlord's consent to non-structural Alterations that do not affect Building Systems cannot be unreasonably withheld. Decorative and workstation/data work up to $250,000 (rising to $400,000 after expansion, both CPI-adjusted) needs no consent, and Landlord is deemed to consent if it does not respond after a reminder notice.
positions.proposed_response: Require Landlord's consent for all non-decorative Alterations. Reduce the consent-free cap to a small per-project amount, with no expansion step-up, and keep the exclusion of anything touching Building Systems or structure. Delete the deemed-consent provision in Section 8.02(i).
quotes: Landlord will not unreasonably withhold or delay approval of written requests of Tenant to make Alterations that (1) do not affect the Building’s exterior

Landlord’s consent shall not be required with respect to Non-Material Alterations which (w) do not require a building permit or a change in the certificate of occupancy for the Building, (x) do not cost in excess of (I) $250,000.00 (Subject to CPI Increases) or (II) from and after the Expansion Space Inclusion Date, $400,000.00 (Subject to CPI Increases)
then Landlord shall be deemed to have consented to the Alteration in question and the Tenant’s Plans with respect thereto.
positions.why: The standard requires consent for all non-decorative work. Here consent is reasonableness-limited for all non-structural, non-systems work, the consent-free threshold is high, and a deemed-approval mechanism applies. Contractor approval and recovery of Landlord's review costs (8.02(x)) are broadly consistent.

positions.lease_says: Tenant must remove listed Specialty Alterations (such as kitchens, raised floors, vaults and slab penetrations) at its cost, but one internal staircase is excluded, supplemental HVAC is not listed, and non-listed items escape removal if Landlord fails to designate them after Tenant's time-sensitive inquiry notice.
positions.proposed_response: Add supplemental HVAC to the Specialty Alterations list and delete the single-staircase carve-out. Delete Section 8.01(iv) so that removal of specialty alterations applies whether or not Landlord designated them at the time of consent.
quotes: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Lease to the contrary, Tenant shall not be obligated to remove any Alterations, except, subject to the provisions of this Section 8.01(iii) and Section 12.01, Specialty Alterations.
internal staircases (provided, that one internal staircase in the Premises shall not constitute a Specialty Alteration, but any additional internal staircase shall constitute a Specialty Alteration)
then, in either case, Tenant shall not be required to remove or pay for the removal of such Alterations which are not so designated as Specialty Alterations.
positions.why: The standard requires removal of all specialty alterations whether or not designated. Here one internal staircase is carved out, supplemental HVAC is not enumerated, and Landlord loses the removal right for non-listed items if it misses the 8.01(iv) designation window.

positions.lease_says: From the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant pays its Percentage of all Expenses each Expense Year, with no base year and no cap, and Expenses are grossed up for unfurnished services.
quotes: an amount (such amount being referred to herein as the “Expense Payment”) equal to the Percentage of the Expenses for such Expense Year (or portion thereof).

the Expenses for such Expense Year shall be increased by an amount equal to the additional expenses which would reasonably have been incurred during such Expense Year by Landlord if Landlord had at its own expense furnished such item of work or service to the entire Project.
positions.why: Tenant pays its share of total Expenses rather than only increases over a base year, with no cap, which gives Landlord more than the standard. The Percentage definition is partly redacted, but this does not affect the structure.

positions.lease_says: From the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant pays Tenant's Share of all Real Estate Taxes, computed without the benefit of abatements or exemptions.
quotes: Tenant shall pay to Landlord, as Additional Rent for each Tax Year occurring during the Term, an amount equal to Tenant’s Share of the Real Estate Taxes for such Tax Year
